ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the rhombus ABCD, point E is a point on side AB, and $DE=AD$. Connect EC. If $\angle ADE = 40^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BCE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus,\\
thus $AD=CD$, $\angle A=\angle BCD$, $CD\parallel AB$,\\
since $DE=AD$, $\angle ADE=40^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle DAE=\angle DEA=70^\circ$,\\
since $CD\parallel AB$,\\
thus $\angle CDE=\angle DEA=70^\circ$, and $DE=DC=DA$,\\
thus $\angle DCE=55^\circ$,\\
since $\angle DCB=\angle DAE=70^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BCE=\angle DCB-\angle DCE=\boxed{15^\circ}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the rhombus ABCD, point E lies on side AB, and DE = AD. Connect EC. If ∠ADE = 40°, what is the measure of ∠BCE?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Since ABCD is a rhombus: AD = CD and CD ∥ AB. Given DE = AD and ∠ADE = 40°, triangle ADE is isosceles, so ∠DAE = ∠DEA = 70°. Because CD ∥ AB, ∠CDE = ∠DEA = 70°. Also DE = DC = DA, so ∠DCE = 55°. And ∠DCB = ∠DAE = 70°. Therefore, ∠BCE = ∠DCB - ∠DCE = 15°.

First describe the image: In the figure, ABCD is drawn as a rhombus, AB is below, DC is above and parallel to AB; A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, D is at the upper left, and C is at the upper right. Point E is located on the bottom side AB, and DE and EC are connected in the figure.

Then reason: It is known that DE = AD, and ∠ADE = 40°, so triangle ADE is an isosceles triangle, with vertex angle 40°, therefore the two base angles ∠DAE and ∠DEA are both (180° - 40°) / 2 = 70°. Because in the rhombus CD ∥ AB, and AE is on AB, it can be obtained that ∠CDE = ∠DEA = 70°. Also because ABCD is a rhombus, AD = CD; it is known that DE = AD, so DE = DC. Therefore triangle DCE is also an isosceles triangle, and the vertex angle ∠CDE = 70°, so ∠DCE = (180° - 70°) / 2 = 55°. The opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, or from the parallel relationship it can be obtained that ∠DCB = ∠DAE = 70°. Thus ∠BCE = ∠DCB - ∠DCE = 70° - 55° = 15°.
